- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) and forecast spikes upward, reduce the peak overshoot by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and forecast declines sharply, avoid underestimating the depth of correction — add 2–5% buffer to prevent premature bottoming.
- Model tends to overestimate short-term volatility in high-sentiment periods — dampen forecast variance by 15–20% when sentiment >0.7.
- In multi-day sentiment shifts (e.g., from bullish to bearish), model often lags — adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to align with sentiment reversal.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is trending, model overfits recent momentum — apply mean reversion bias: subtract 1–3% from forecast if price has moved >5% from 10-day average.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overestimates price in early period (first 5–7 days) — reduce forecast by 2–5% for first 7 days if sentiment is positive.
- If sentiment is consistently positive over 3+ days, model tends to overcorrect — apply downward bias of 3–5% in final 5–7 days of forecast.
